To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the cleaning efficacy of aqueous and hydrocarbon solvent‐based cleaning systems is comparable, (ii) surfactant residues can be detected in the paint film following aqueous cleaning and (iii), in some instances, pigment modifications occur during cleaning.
the wet cleaning of artists' acrylic paint model films on canvas was found to be effective in the removal of the artificial soiling applied.

the use of surfactants in aqueous cleaning systems can be beneficial for the conservation of acrylic emulsion paintings and that the use of chelating agents in aqueous cleaning formulations can have detrimental effects.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and optimisation of cleaning methods for acrylic emulsion paints.
the conservation of acrylic emulsion paints.
the impact of wet cleaning methods on artists' acrylic emulsions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the cleaning systems tested here have a limited effect on the paint film.
the cleaning treatments examined here are not detrimental to artists' acrylic paint, but that there is a need for caution when using some of them.
the use of wet cleaning methods on model artists' acrylic emulsions is not recommended.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
XPS, NIXAFS and ATRAFTIR are powerful tools to study and understand the impact of wet cleaning on artists' acrylic paint surfaces.
the combination of the three techniques used provided a more complete understanding of the cleaning process than could be achieved with any of them individually.

the cleaning efficacy of the aqueous cleaning methods tested was comparable to the hydrocarbon solvent systems, and that the cleaning systems with the addition of chelating agents, surfactants and/or microemulsion systems were the most effective in removing soiling from the model paint films, but also had the potential to leave residues on the paint surface.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the choice of wet cleaning system is critical to the long‐term stability of artists' acrylic paints.
the combination of the three techniques is necessary to understand the surface modifications that may result from wet cleaning.

the use of X‐ray spectroscopic techniques, particularly in combination, can provide valuable information to support the development of effective cleaning treatments and their optimisation for the conservation of acrylic emulsion paint films.
